readme: What kit each squad wore, for whoever is drawing the sticker cards. Keyed by squad id
(`<code>-<year>`), so it is per tournament rather than per nation: a nation's colours
move, and the card is one player at one World Cup.
Read by `npm run ratings:sync`, which merges it into docs/missing-sticker-art.html.
`numberOnFront` says whether the shirt carries the player's number on the CHEST as well
as the back, which the drawing prompt has to state either way. Modern national shirts do
and every side before the 1990s did not.
A squad with no entry prints as 'not recorded' rather than being guessed at, and only
squads that owe a card need one. `npm run checks` fails on an entry whose key is not a
real squad, so a typo cannot sit here looking like data.
`confidence` says how much weight to put on it, and it is the point of the file:
verified - checked against a source or against art already shipped for that squad
known    - long-established colours for that side at that tournament
standard - the nation's usual colours, NOT the specific release worn that year
Hex values are for the swatch, so they are the readable middle of each colour rather

shirt.name: Canary yellow, green collar and cuffs

bra-1970.note: Matches the cards already drawn for this squad (Pele, Jairzinho): open V collar in dark green, CBD shield on the left breast.

ger-1970.note: As drawn on the shipped Beckenbauer 1974 card: DFB roundel on the left breast, no maker's stripes on the shirt body.

eng-1970.note: All white, NOT the usual navy shorts: Umbro made the Mexico kit in perforated Airtex and England wore white shorts to take less heat. The red change shirt was swapped for sky blue for the same reason.

ned-1974.note: Adidas, with black stripes down the sleeve (see the note on Cruyff: his shirt carried two of them, not three).

pol-1974.note: The white eagle crest on the left breast. 1974 is where Poland settled on white at home and red away.

shirt.name: Blue with red and white pinstripes

fra-1982.note: The Adidas shirt with fine red and white pinstripes on blue, tricolour V neck, gold cockerel crest.

bra-1982.note: Topolino era: same colours as 1970, crew neck rather than a collar.

shirt.name: White with a black, red and gold chest band

ger-1982.note: The band across the chest is the whole character of this shirt; get it in and the card reads as 1982 immediately.

fra-1986.note: Plainer than 1982: no pinstripes, red and white banding at the collar and cuffs.

esp-1986.note: Red shirt over dark shorts is the Spanish constant; the crest sits on the left breast.

eng-1986.note: Navy shorts are back by 1986, so this is NOT the all-white 1970 look.

den-1986.note: The Hummel shirt: the two halves carry red and white pinstripes at different weights, with chevrons on the sleeves. The pattern is the card.

urs-1986.note: Adidas. The lettering rather than a crest is what dates it.

shirt.name: Red, navy sleeve panels and yellow pinstripes

esp-2026.note: The 2026 shirt is reported as red with navy sleeve panels and yellow pinstripes off the flag and crest; the rest is Spain's usual.

mar-2026.note: The green is the pentangle on the flag and it is what stops the card reading as any other red side.

players.ned-1974-14: Cruyff wore TWO sleeve stripes where the rest of the side wore three: he was under contract to Puma and would not carry Adidas's third. Getting this wrong is the one detail people will notice on this card.
players.bel-2026-1: Goalkeeper, so the outfield colours above do not apply to him: he needs a strip that separates from them, which for Belgium has lately meant yellow or grey.
